MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

Fires on the sub-word continuation token immediately following a capital "M" (or "IM") — e.g. "rs/RS" in Mrs./MRS., "HO" in IMHO, "umba" in #mumbaifood, "ár" in Márquez — i.e. it's a positional token-fragment detector after M, and is strongly suppressed when that fragment is "ent"/"ents" (Mentha, Sacraments, Demantec).

L0·N9644unmasked layer
Fires on specific word-internal subword continuation fragments—typically the piece right after a "T"/"t" in a name or technical term (e.g. "abor" in Tabor/tabor, "ento" in dentoalveolar, "aff" in Taffi, "ner" in Hüttner, "ull" in Chee-poe-tull); other "T"+fragment splits ("unn", "ages", "outes", "MP") instead suppress it, so it is keyed to these particular sub-word strings rather than to any semantic content.
